newsitem.title: FRANCE: Netanyahu to call Mubarak on Jerusalem violence.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu to call Mubarak on Jerusalem violence.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he planned to call Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on Wednesday to try to calm Arab violence over Israel's opening of a tunnel under the Old City of Jerusalem.

"I'm going to speak with President Mubarak today because my intention is to calm tensions," Netanyahu told reporters travelling with him in Paris after Israeli troops wounded some 160 Palestinian protesters near the West Bank town of Ramallah.

Netanyahu said he had decided to consult Mubarak before the Ramallah clashes, urging Arab leaders to exercise restraint and be careful with the facts over the disputed tunnel. Asked if he would also call Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, he said: "If there is a need, I will also speak (with Arafat)."
A senior Israeli official travelling with Netanyahu charged that Arafat was behind Wednesday's violence and that Palestinian police had been told not to intervene to prevent violence.

"In Ramallah, there was a deliberate attempt to push the demonstrators towards Israeli soldiers. Apparently, guidelines were given to Palestinian police not to intervene. It looks like a well-organised attempt to apply pressure on us," the official told reporters.
Asked whether he would cut short his trip to Britain, France and Germany, Netanyahu said he only that he was in constant contact with Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai.
